title: Global canonical resolution section transfer
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$, $G$, $I$, $J$, $\alpha$, $h_\alpha$, $c_X$, and $c_Y$ be as follows: $G$ is an abelian etale sheaf on $X$, $I$ resolves $G$, $J$ resolves $g^*G$, $\alpha:I\to g_*J$ preserves the augmentation, and $c_X,c_Y$ are normalized comparisons [def-weil-pbc-etale-resolution-section-canonical-comparison]. For every $q$ and $x\in H^q(I(X))$, $c_Y^q(H^q(T_X)x)=g^*(c_X^q(x))$. Here $T$ is the explicit section transfer [def-weil-pbc-etale-resolution-section-transfer] and pullback is [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

proof.text:
Proof: Represent a homology class by a cycle z, using surjectivity of homologyπ.
The constant-sheaf adjunction and evaluation at 1 give a unique morphism f representing
its underlying section. Naturality of this equivalence and the cycle equation give
f ≫ d = 0. Adjoint α to β : g*I → J. The equation hα identifies the augmentation
of β with the identity of g*G. Exactness of g* makes g*I a resolution of g*G.

Proof: Represent a homology class by a cycle z, using surjectivity of homologyπ.
The constant-sheaf adjunction and evaluation at 1 give a unique morphism f representing
its underlying section. Naturality of this equivalence and the cycle equation give
f ≫ d = 0. Adjoint α to β : g*I → J. The equation hα identifies the augmentation
of β with the identity of g*G. Exactness of g* makes g*I a resolution of g*G.
In the derived category, write I.extMk f using extMk_hom. Apply the exact functor g*
and precompose with the constant-sheaf comparison. The augmentation equation cancels
the two resolution identifications, yielding the Ext class of the cocycle β after g*f.
Under the constant-sheaf adjunction this cocycle evaluates to α at the terminal object
followed by restriction along terminalSectionPullback g. This is exactly the degree-q
map of globalResolutionSectionTransfer. The chain-map equation makes its value a cycle.
Apply cX.global_cocycle and cY.global_cocycle to these representatives, and use naturality
of homologyπ to obtain the claimed equality for z, hence for every class. This argument
uses no positive-degree assumption; zero coefficients and empty schemes cause no change.

from.place: The resolution-section comparison: normalized Hom cocycles, their restriction, and their augmentation-preserving pullback transfer, below the Mayer-Vietoris comparison.

lean.statement: theorem resolutionSection_canonical_transfer_global {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (I : InjectiveResolution G) (J : InjectiveResolution ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).obj G)) (α : I.cocomplex ⟶ ((lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj J.cocomplex) (hα : I.ι.f 0 ≫ α.f 0 = (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).unit.app G ≫ (lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).map (J.ι.f 0)) (cX : ResolutionSectionCanonicalComparison G I) (cY : ResolutionSectionCanonicalComparison ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).obj G) J) : ∀ q x, cY.globalEquiv q (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (globalResolutionSectionTransfer g I.cocomplex J.cocomplex α) q x) = cohomologyMap g G q (cX.globalEquiv q x)
